(This Evening through Sunday)...
Issued at 233 PM EDT Sun Sep 20 2026

A slow moving cold front will remain the focal point for periodic 
convection tonight into early Monday. The front will move south of 
the Ohio River on Monday but isolated showers will remain possible 
into early Tuesday prior to the passage of an upper level wave. Much 
cooler air will overspread the region in the wake of the front. An 
upper low will cutoff over the mid Atlantic during the second half 
of the week...with much drier air being pulled south into the Ohio 
Valley. This will result in pleasant early Fall conditions late this 
week into the upcoming weekend. 

Rest of Today through Tuesday Night

Mid and high level clouds continue to overspread the region this 
afternoon with a frontal boundary draped across central Indiana. 
Temperatures varied across the boundary...ranging from the mid 70s 
over north central Indiana to near 90 along our southern border at 
18Z.

The frontal boundary will serve as a focal point for renewed 
convective development late today into tonight as a surface wave 
rides along it. Showers over northwest Indiana will drift east with 
additional development back to the west across Illinois. While 
initial movement should keep the bulk of the showers and storms 
largely to the north of the forecast area...expect a gradual 
southern drift into the northeast half of the forecast area by early 
evening with additional showers and storms riding along the boundary 
overnight. 

There remains a non-zero threat for a few severe storms but overall 
the thermodynamics remain unimpressive. Peak CAPE values are only at 
about 1000 j/kg with limited BL shear. There is a narrow window 
between now and 22-23Z where MLCAPE values may nudge up slightly in 
an axis along and just north of the front across the northern half 
of the forecast area where any stronger cell that can develop may 
carry an isolated damaging wind risk. All in all though...the 
severe risk appears very low into this evening.

The greater threat from convection will be locally heavy rainfall as 
an axis of PWATs in excess of 1.75 inches pivots south across the 
area tonight. Model soundings continue to advertise a deep warm layer 
up to near 500mb and the presence of a modest westerly low level jet 
tonight all support potential for efficient rainfall rates and some 
backbuilding of showers and storms in the vicinity of the boundary. 
Briefly considered a Flood Watch over far northeast portions of the 
forecast area for tonight but the bulk of the heavier rainfall over 
the last 72 hours has bypassed us to the north and east. 1- and 3-
hour flash flood guidance numbers are manageable and also argue 
against a Flood Watch. Will certainly monitor convective trends into 
the evening but will not carry any flood headlines at this time.

Showers will linger into Monday but coverage will steadily decrease 
throughout the day as the front shifts into the Tennessee Valley. 
Abundant moisture will persist through the boundary layer however 
trapped beneath a stout inversion. This will keep skies mostly 
cloudy through Monday night and likely even into Tuesday as an upper 
wave approaches from the northwest. Cannot rule out a few showers 
Monday night and Tuesday but will be isolated at best with moisture 
largely confined to the boundary layer. A decrease in clouds will 
commence Tuesday night as drier air attempts to advect south on the 
back side of the departing wave aloft. The development of an upper 
low over the eastern Great Lakes Tuesday night may serve however to 
delay more substantial clearing from the west.

Temps...today will be the last very warm day as the passage of the 
front by early Monday will advect much cooler air into the region 
from the north. Low level thermals support highs in the upper 60s 
north to near 80 in the lower Wabash Valley Monday with upper 60s to 
lower 70s Tuesday. The current forecast high of 69 degrees for KIND 
for Tuesday would be the first sub-70 degree day since May 23. Lows 
will transition down into the lower and middle 50s by MOnday/Tuesday 
nights as well.

Wednesday through Sunday

Strong signals in the extended model suite suggest the 
aforementioned upper low will amplify and become cutoff from the 
mean flow aloft over the Mid Atlantic region during the second half 
of the week. Cool E/NE flow and at least some lingering cloud cover 
on the back side of the developing cutoff low will maintain below 
normal temperatures Wednesday and for parts of the area Thursday as 
well with highs ranging from the upper 60s to the mid 70s from 
northeast to southwest. A few light showers cannot be entirely ruled 
out over far eastern portions of the forecast area Wednesday but 
confidence is far too low for a mention in the forecast as better 
forcing aloft will be east of the region.
